title: The dragging is what hurts
literal_meaning: Being taken by a tiger does not hurt; the dragging hurts.
explanation: The line sets being taken by a tiger beside the discomfort of being dragged. The dictionary quotes it under dragging along the ground. Our reading hears an exaggerated complaint that singles out one part of a larger ordeal. It does not measure pain or establish that the larger danger is harmless; no actual encounter or speaker is identified.
meaning_odia: ବାଘ ନେବା ସହ ଭୂମିରେ ଘୋଷାରି ନେବାର କଷ୍ଟକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଭୂମିରେ ଟାଣିନେବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ବଡ଼ ଦୁର୍ଦ୍ଦଶାର ଗୋଟିଏ ଅଂଶକୁ ବାଛି ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତିରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରାଯାଏ। ଏହା ଯନ୍ତ୍ରଣାର ମାପ ନୁହେଁ ବା ବଡ଼ ବିପଦ ନିରାପଦ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରକୃତ ଘଟଣା ବା ବକ୍ତା ଚିହ୍ନଟ ହୋଇନାହାନ୍ତି।
english_summary: Our reading singles out one discomfort within an exaggerated ordeal.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଅତିଶୟ ଦୁର୍ଦ୍ଦଶା ଭିତରୁ ଗୋଟିଏ କଷ୍ଟ ଅଭିଯୋଗର କେନ୍ଦ୍ର।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଲମ୍ବା ଯାତ୍ରାର ସବୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଭଙ୍ଗା ବ୍ୟାଗ୍ ଟାଣିବା କଥାଟି ଜଣେ ବାରମ୍ବାର କହିଲେ। / A traveller keeps returning to the broken bag amid a difficult journey. This comparison is invented.
cultural_context: Exact fused ବାଘନବା remains unchanged. The quoted contrast is rhetorical, not medical or wildlife advice. Later road and laziness senses do not supply this saying’s meaning.
